name: LP-EM-CC2340R5 LaunchPad development kit
sources: CC2340R family data sheet SWRS272F (features list; read 2026-10-07); LP-EM-CC2340R5 quick start guide SWRU588A (board overview, BoosterPack pinout, box contents; read 2026-10-07); SimpleLink Low Power F3 SDK 9.21 board file LP_EM_CC2340R5.syscfg.json (LEDs, buttons, header pins)

columns.head: The chip: CC2340R5
items: Processor: Arm Cortex-M0+
Runs the program, up to 48 million steps a second (48 MHz)
Chip: 2.4 GHz radio
Bluetooth Low Energy, Zigbee and Thread, up to +8 dBm. This is what the chip is for
Flash: 512 kB
Holds the program and the radio stack. Kept when the power is off
RAM: 36 kB
Working memory. The Bluetooth stack takes most of it, so a sensor app gets what is left
Power: 1.71 to 3.8 V
3.3 V from the debug probe on this board, so 5 V parts need care

columns.head: Connections inside the chip
items: GPIO: up to 26 pads
Plain on/off pins (TI calls them DIO). 22 of them reach the board's headers
UART: 1 / SPI: 1 / I2C: 1
Serial text / fast bus for displays and memory / two-wire bus for sensors. Only one of each
ADC: 12-bit
Measures a voltage in 4,096 steps, up to 12 inputs
Timers: 3 x 16-bit, 1 x 24-bit
PWM, timing a pulse, counting a knob (quadrature decode), making an IR carrier
Chip: AES and random numbers in hardware
Hardware for encryption, which the radio stacks use

columns.head: On the board, and missing
items: On the board
Red LED (DIO14), green LED (DIO15), two buttons (DIO10, DIO9), 1 MB SPI flash, chip antenna
Headers
40-pin BoosterPack layout (J1 to J4); several positions are not connected
Debug probe: none on the board
Needs an LP-XDS110ET or LP-XDS110 probe on its edge connector, sold separately. The probe also powers it
Watch out
Only one I2C bus: every Qwiic sensor shares DIO24 (SCL) and DIO0 (SDA). No pull-up resistors found on the board
